task.description:
WF-03 Step 4b -- hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's regression coverage for ISS-0106. Re-derive your verdict from the test file and the spec themselves. Reading step-04-regression-test.json's result.summary and echoing it back is not validation, it is copying a claim (core-directives.md, 'Every producing step has a validating step').

WHAT IS UNDER TEST: a new mix task, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex, which reads .tool-versions and prints an advisory toolchain warning. Its specification is Part A item 3 of the design at lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md, and the properties it must have come from the decision record's amendment -- the check is adopted ONLY as an unsuppressible warning that never alters another check's exit code, so tests asserting those two properties are load-bearing rather than decorative.

Deliberately NOT covered by ExUnit, by ORCH's instruction, so do not report it as missing coverage: the fix's Part B (four reformatted files) and Part C (sixteen struct-update annotations). Both are already enforced by exit-code gates in the letflow.check alias, and duplicating an exit-code gate in ExUnit would be redundant machinery. Their WF-03-mandated fail-then-pass evidence belongs in the spec as measured gate exit codes instead -- CHECK THAT IT IS THERE and that the numbers were measured rather than quoted.

FOUR THINGS DESERVE MORE THAN A CHECKLIST PASS:

  1. **VACUITY.** The single most valuable thing you can do is find a test that would pass against a WRONG implementation. This project has been bitten by exactly that before: a prior run's security test seeded values that never reached any input the function under test could observe, making every refutation trivially true against every possible implementation, and it took a validator FAIL to catch. TEST-DESIGNER reports guarding against this by MUTATION-testing three variants of the shipped logic -- a naive full-string OTP comparison (17/30 pass), an unstripped -otp-NN suffix (24/30), and warnings routed to stdout (11/30). Those numbers are the strongest evidence in this step if true. Verify at least one mutant yourself by actually applying it and running the tests, rather than accepting the count. If a mutant you apply does NOT fail the tests it should, that is a vacuity finding and grounds to FAIL.

  2. **THE F7 FINDING, which TEST-DESIGNER reported rather than papered over.** F7's condition is File.cwd/0 returning an error, and it reports that Windows will not let a process delete its own working directory, so the failure mode has no portable external trigger here; two alternative induction routes were probed and rejected with measured reasons. Its test therefore attempts the real induction and asserts the real F7 output where the OS permits it, and asserts a structural guarantee otherwise. YOUR JOB: determine whether the structural branch is a genuine assertion or a dressed-up no-op. A branch that merely asserts a string exists in the source file is much weaker than one that constrains behaviour -- rule on which this is, and say whether the test would actually catch a regression in F7's handling on this host. Note the correct disposition if it is weak is a stated coverage limitation, NOT an invented stub and NOT a public seam added to the module (that would be a CODE-DESIGNER change).

  3. **CROSS-HOST DURABILITY.** ISS-0106 is fundamentally a cross-host problem, so a test that only passes on this host's toolchain would make the fix a new instance of the very class it resolves. Verify independently that no assertion depends on a hardcoded version string, and that the fixtures derive their expectations from the RUNNING toolchain read at runtime. Check specifically that the tests would pass on a host running Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27 -- reason about it concretely from the fixture construction, and say so either way.

  4. **THE 255-CHARACTER NAME CAP.** Re-run the mechanical length measurement YOURSELF over every describe/test pair in the new file rather than accepting the reported maximum of 75. docs/anti-patterns.md records four suite-breaking recurrences of this exact class and states explicitly that documentation alone has not prevented it, so an independent measurement here is the mechanical check that entry asks for. Report your own measured maximum.

Also check the ordinary things: every acceptance criterion in step-04-regression-test.json (AC1..AC11) genuinely met; no test skipped or tagged out; fixtures isolated and self-sufficient; and the file does not adopt the nested-`mix test` pattern that makes the pre-existing Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest time out.

Do NOT gate on the suite's ~13-14 pre-existing failures elsewhere (Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest, Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest). Attribution is TEST-RUNNER's at the next step.

Cross-host durability verified independently: no hardcoded version literals, expectations derived from the running toolchain, and a concrete statement of whether these tests would pass on an Elixir 1.18.3 / OTP 27 host

Confirmation that no test is skipped, excluded or tagged out, and that fixtures are isolated and self-sufficient
Confirmation that the spec carries the Part B and Part C fail-then-pass gate evidence, and that those exit codes were measured at main vs HEAD rather than quoted from an earlier step

No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step -- and any mutant you applied is reverted, with the revert verified and stated

result.summary: PASS. Verdict re-derived by reading test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs, test/specs/ISS-0106.md and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex directly and by running measurements myself; TEST-DESIGNER's step-04 result.summary was not used as evidence. BASELINE reproduced: 'Result: 30 passed', exit 0. VACUITY (the priority item) -- I applied TWO of the three reported mutants to the shipped module in this checkout and ran the file. Mutant A (expected_otp_major/1 returns the token whole, i.e. the naive full-string OTP comparison): 'Result: 17/30 passed', 13 failures, with T-M2 ('matching pin a full erlang pin matches a major-only OTP release') and T-M3 ('the -otp-NN suffix is discarded and never compared') both among the failures. Mutant C (warn_block/2 uses IO.puts(&1) instead of IO.puts(:stderr, &1)): 'Result: 11/30 passed', 19 failures, with T-I1, T-I3, T-I4 and every warning-path test failing. Both counts reproduce TEST-DESIGNER's reported figures exactly (17/30 and 11/30), which corroborates the third (24/30) I did not run. The tests genuinely discriminate against a wrong implementation -- they are not tautological. Both mutants reverted via 'git checkout --'; module SHA1 back to the pristine edf0dc350292ebb5b5f653222568737dc0e02a6e, 'git status --porcelain lib/ test/' empty, and the file re-runs 30 passed. NAME LENGTH measured by me, not accepted: extracted all 30 ExUnit-constructed names from 'mix test --trace' output; 30 pairs found; MAX = 75 chars ('test failure modes F7 an unavailable working directory warns and returns ok'), against a 200-char working limit and ExUnit's 255-char hard cap. Matches the reported figure. CROSS-HOST: grep for version-like literals in the test file returns only three hits, none of them an assertion -- line 35 is moduledoc prose, lines 321/324 are 'nodejs 22.1.0' and 'python 3.12.1' inside the T-P1 fixture, deliberately other-tool lines the task ignores by design and never compares. Every fixture is built from running_elixir/0 (System.version/0) and running_otp/0 (List.to_string(:erlang.system_info(:otp_release))), which are functions evaluated at run time, not module attributes frozen at compile time; off_pin/1 appends '9', so an off-pin fixture differs from the running value in LENGTH and can never coincide with it on any host. The one version-shaped literal '.7.13' is only ever a suffix on running_otp(). Traced concretely for an Elixir 1.18.3 / OTP 27 host: matching_pin becomes 'elixir 1.18.3-otp-27 / erlang 27.7.13' -> expected_elixir '1.18.3' == running, expected_otp_major '27' == running -> T-M1/T-M2/T-M3 pass; off_pin gives '1.18.39' and '279', both unequal by construction -> T-X1..T-X3 pass. These tests pass on 1.18.3/OTP 27. SKIP/EXCLUDE: grep for @tag/@moduletag/:skip/exclude across the test file, test/test_helper.exs and mix.exs returns nothing; run output shows 30 passed with no skipped and no excluded. FIXTURES: each test builds its own temp dir via fresh_dir/0 keyed on System.unique_integer([:positive]) with an on_exit rm_rf; no test depends on another having run; T-I3 saves and restores Mix.shell/0 and T-I4 saves and restores MIX_QUIET, both via on_exit. async: false is correct and sufficient -- ExUnit runs sync modules after all async modules, so the VM-wide File.cd! cannot interleave. No hardcoded secret or connection string. The file does NOT adopt the nested-'mix test' pattern -- grep for System.cmd/Mix.Task.run/Port.open/'mix test' in it returns nothing, so it does not share Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest's timeout mode. PARTS B/C GATE EVIDENCE re-measured by me rather than read: pre-fix, main's versions of the four files extracted with 'git show main:<path>' and run through 'mix format --check-formatted' -> exit 1, naming exactly those four (pin_resolver_test.exs, pin_resolver.ex, pin_rebind_test.exs, variable_merge.ex); post-fix at HEAD 'mix format --check-formatted' -> exit 0. 'MIX_ENV=test mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors' at HEAD -> exit 0 with 0 'is expected on struct update' warnings; the diff main...HEAD adds exactly 16 '%Struct{} =' annotation bind sites, matching the design's M2. Spec section 2 states the measurement method (a throwaway git worktree of main with a private MIX_BUILD_PATH) and presents the numbers as taken during step 4, not quoted from step 2 or 3. AC1..AC11 individual verdicts: AC1 MET (spec section 2 for B/C, section 4 for A). AC2 MET (test/mix/tasks/ placement matching letflow_check_test_test.exs; compiles; underscore naming already ratified by ORCH in this handoff's orch_correction). AC3 MET and independently measured -- mutant A is exactly the naive comparison and takes the file to 17/30. AC4 MET (T-X1/X2/X3 assert the WHOLE rendered row via elixir_row/3 and otp_row/4 helpers, not a bare '=~ running'; TEST-DESIGNER's own comment on T-X1 identifies the vacuity trap that the running version is a prefix of the off-pin one, and avoids it -- this is the anti-vacuity care this gate looks for). AC5 MET (T-P1 asserts comments/blanks/other tools are ignored SILENTLY via stderr == ''; T-F5a/b assert malformed lines are quoted). AC6 MET for F1-F6 and F8 -- each asserts a message AND result == :ok; MET WITH A STATED LIMITATION for F7, see the MINOR issue below. AC7 MET (T-I1 stderr-not-stdout, T-I2 args ignored, T-I3 quiet shell, T-I4 MIX_QUIET, T-I5 structural no-abort grep, T-I6 :ok sweep over nine fixture shapes). AC8 MET (75 chars, my own measurement). AC9 MET (30 passed reproduced by me). AC10 MET -- step 4's commit 36b1be2 touches only test/specs/ISS-0106.md, the test file, and handoffs/; nothing under lib/. AC11 MET (see CROSS-HOST above). T-F7 RULING: a genuine assertion, but a WEAK one on this host, and correctly disposed of. It is not a no-op -- the not-induced branch can fail, and would fail if the F7 clause or its message string were deleted or if File.cwd/0 were swapped for File.cwd!/0. But it is a source-TEXT check, not a behavioural one, and on Windows it verifies no F7 behaviour at all: it would NOT catch an F7 branch that returns something other than :ok, that emits the wrong block title, that routes to stdout instead of stderr, that breaks on inspect(reason), or that becomes unreachable through clause reordering. It is also very nearly subsumed by T-I5, which already asserts 'File.cwd()' and refutes 'File.cwd!' over the same stripped source -- its only incremental content is 'assert code =~ "Could not determine the project directory"'. Per this handoff's own guidance the correct disposition for a weak branch is a stated coverage limitation, and the spec does state it, in section 3.6, with the two rejected alternative inductions and their measured reasons ({:error, :eacces} on rm_rf of own cwd; :eio on the over-long-cwd route). No stub was invented and no public seam was added to the module. The behavioural branch will be taken on any POSIX host, so F7 does get real behavioural coverage in CI/hetzner. Not grounds to FAIL. Worth noting that the test's own comment and spec section 3.6 both say 'Either way it asserts something that a regression would break' -- true, but it understates how much narrower the structural branch is; recorded as MINOR so the wording is sharpened rather than left to read as parity between the branches. Two positive notes on anti-vacuity design: T-I5's module_code/0 helper is self-guarding -- if the doc-stripping ever degenerated to an empty string, its refutes would pass trivially but its two asserts ('File.cwd()', 'File.read(path)') would fail, so the test cannot go silently vacuous; and the toggle over lines containing triple-quote is balanced in the module (4 occurrences, all doc delimiters), so nothing executable is stripped. No file outside handoffs/ was modified by this step: working tree shows only ORCH's own handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json and untracked docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml, all left alone, plus this handoff file. Scratch files were written to scratch/ and removed. No docker compose was run.

issues.description: T-F7's not-induced (Windows) branch is a source-text assertion, not a behavioural one, and is almost entirely subsumed by T-I5 -- its only incremental assertion is the presence of the 'Could not determine the project directory' string. It would not catch an F7 branch that returns non-:ok, emits the wrong title, routes to stdout, or becomes unreachable. This is accepted as a stated coverage limitation (correctly reported by TEST-DESIGNER, correctly NOT worked around with a stub or a public seam), but test/specs/ISS-0106.md section 3.6 and the test's own comment both say 'either branch asserts something a regression would break' without noting the asymmetry. Suggest a one-line wording change in section 3.6 stating plainly that on Windows F7 has structural coverage only and no behavioural coverage. Not a blocker and no rework requested; F7 gets real behavioural coverage on any POSIX host, where the induction succeeds.

Informational, for TEST-RUNNER at the next step: I did not run the full suite and make no attribution of the ~13-14 pre-existing failures in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest and Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest. The new file is confirmed not to share their nested-'mix test' failure mode.
